title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 1–4): Grothendieck is setting up a combinatorial-axiomatic framework for 'tame' (modérée) topology. A space X carries a given set 𝓕 of 'figures'. A figure F is a finite stratification of a closed subset |F| = ∪X_i of X. It is identified with the set of its closed strata X_i, so F ⊂ 𝓟_f(X). The strata satisfy conditions a)–f) from the previous page:
- int(X_i) = X_i∖∂X_i is a connected manifold;
- ∂X_i is a union of strata;
- X_i ∩ X_j is a union of strata.
The strata form a poset Σ_F under inclusion.

This page:
(1) Sub-figures. F' is a sub-figure of F if every stratum of F' is a stratum of F, i.e. F' ⊂ F as sets of closed subsets. Hence |F'| ⊂ |F|.
(2) NB (closure property). If X_i ∈ F' and Y_j ∈ F with Y_j ⊂ X_i, then Y_j ∈ F'. A sub-figure is therefore automatically downward closed in Σ_F.
(3) Ordering. Write F' ≤ F; this is an order relation on 𝓕.
(4) Sub-figures as order ideals. Sub-figures of F correspond bijectively to the subsets Φ (= Σ_{F'}) of Σ_F such that i ∈ Φ and j ≤ i imply j ∈ Φ. These are the order ideals (lower sets), i.e. the closed sets of the Alexandrov-type topology on the finite poset Σ_F. The smallest closed set containing i is Σ_{≤i}.
(5) Elementary figures (marginal note dated 11.6, 'je dirai plutôt', replacing the crossed-out 'irréductible'). A figure is elementary if it has a maximal stratum, i.e. Σ_F has a greatest element. Geometrically this is a closed cell-like stratum together with the induced stratification of its boundary. 𝓕_él denotes the set of elementary figures.
(6) Statement begun here, finished on p. 4. The elementary sub-figures of F correspond 1-1 to the strata of F, via X_i ↦ Σ_{≤i}.

Next page: F is recovered from its set Σ'_F ⊂ 𝓕_él of elementary sub-figures. 𝓕_él is ordered by inclusion, and figures correspond to certain (finite) closed, i.e. down-closed, subsets of 𝓕_él. Inclusion of figures becomes inclusion of these subsets.

Purpose: replace geometric stratified objects by a purely order-theoretic gadget. The global poset of 'cells' 𝓕_él carries an Alexandrov topology, and figures are finite closed subsets of it. This is the face-poset description of regular CW / stratified complexes, as a step toward a foundation of tame topology (Esquisse d'un programme, §5).
errors: The NB (downward closedness) is stated without proof; the attempted proof is crossed out. It is true under the axioms: int(Y_j) is a nonempty subset of X_i, and X_i is the disjoint union of the open parts of the F'-strata it contains. These are also strata of F, and distinct strata of F have disjoint open parts, so Y_j must equal one of them.

The bijection 'sub-figures ↔ down-closed subsets of Σ_F' requires that the union of the strata in any lower set is again a figure belonging to the given set 𝓕. Conditions a)–f) are inherited, since boundaries and intersections only involve smaller strata. However, membership in 𝓕 is an extra stability hypothesis on 𝓕 that is not stated. The status of the empty set as a figure is also left implicit.

On p. 4, 'figures = closed subsets of 𝓕_él' is only correct for finite lower sets that are realized as the elementary sub-figures of a single figure. Not every finite lower set of 𝓕_él is of that form, because elementary figures in different positions need not glue to a figure. This compatibility condition is missing.

ideas.what: Figure (stratified closed subset) identified with its set of closed strata; sub-figure = subset of strata
ideas.modern_name: Stratified subcomplex / sub-stratification of a (regular) cell or Whitney-type stratified complex
ideas.where_published: Tame-topology program sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6; this formalism not published

ideas.what: Sub-figures of F ↔ lower sets (Alexandrov-closed sets) of the strata poset Σ_F
ideas.modern_name: Subcomplexes ↔ down-closed subsets of the face poset; Alexandrov topology on a finite poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937); for regular CW complexes, standard (e.g. Björner 1984)

ideas.what: Elementary figure = figure with a greatest stratum; elementary sub-figures ↔ strata; a figure is determined by its elementary sub-figures
ideas.modern_name: Closed cells / principal down-sets Σ_{≤i}; a complex as a colimit (union) of its closed cells; cellular stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (regular CW theory; cf. Tamaki's cellular stratified spaces for a modern axiomatization)

ideas.what: Global poset 𝓕_él of all elementary figures in X, with figures as certain finite closed subsets
ideas.modern_name: Global 'cell poset' / site of elementary pieces of a tame structure; analogous to cell decompositions in o-minimal structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimal cell decomposition: van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (1980s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) announces tame topology but not this formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins axiomatizing a tame topology through a given set 𝓕 of stratified 'figures' in X, recoded order-theoretically as finite closed subsets of a global poset of elementary figures. This is a combinatorial, poset-based foundation, distinct in flavor from o-minimal definable-set axiomatics. The program is not developed in the published record. It is mainly of historical interest, since the individual steps on this page are standard.
missed.quote: figure élémentaire : qui a une strate maximale i.e. Σ_F a un plus grand élément. Soit 𝓕_él l'ens des figures élémentaires.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents Grothendieck's concrete 1986 approach to the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse. It is comparable with o-minimality and with cellular/conical stratified-space frameworks (exit-path categories, Lurie/Ayala–Francis–Tanaka), where stratified objects are also encoded by posets.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is standard: subcomplexes correspond to lower sets of the face poset, and closed cells are principal down-sets. The only interest is historical, as a dated (11 June 1986) glimpse of the foundational set-up for Grothendieck's tame topology program.
transcription_corrections: Left margin: likely '11.6. Je dirai plutôt' (11 June; 'plutôt', not 'plus tôt'), introducing 'figure élémentaire' in place of the crossed-out '"irréductible"'.
Line 4: the crossed-out words after 'Dans' are probably 'le rapport' (or 'ce cas'), and the crossed-out σ(F) precedes '|F'| ⊂ |F|'. The surviving text reads roughly 'Dans ce cas on a |F'| ⊂ |F|'.

The parenthetical after the lower-set condition reads roughly '("idéaux" [replacing crossed-out 'fermées'] de l'ens. ordonné, pour la top. ... ; les Σ_{≤i} ...)'. It refers to the closed sets of the Alexandrov topology generated by the Σ_{≤i}. The exact wording is uncertain; 'communément bien déterminée' is doubtful.
The marginal insertion 'sur Σ_F = Σ' may read 'sous Σ_F ⊂ Σ' (i.e. Σ_F as a part of the global Σ); uncertain.
The insertion over the line reads '(= Σ_{F'})' after Φ, and 'i, j ∈ Σ_F' is inserted above the condition; the transcription is essentially right here.
